seat.BEST_WHY: Frames 2 and 3 are the same render to within measurement (max per-channel pixel delta of 5, confined to the lower-right floor; visually indistinguishable). I put 2 ahead because 3 is fractionally brighter in the already-overexposed floor right of the figure, i.e. marginally more blown out. What is well made: the wall face band running under the dark wall-top at y≈420–460 (x 180–750) is a distinct surface from the wall-top above it and the floor below it — brown timber-and-stone with driven iron pins at x≈300, 400, 460, 590, 690 and a small strapped bracket at x≈340, so the "repaired with pins and salvaged timber" read is in the art, not the caption. The long crack on the floor starting at the plinth (x≈290, y≈600) and running to x≈560 crosses tile joints rather than stopping at them, so the flagstones read as one cracked floor rather than a stamped tile. Floor scratches vary per stone (compare the stone under the figure with the one under the brazier). The lashed timber bundle at (390–500, 590–640) is drawn straight top-down, matching the floor's projection. The light is one warm source with a cool ambient in the dark, and the falloff is continuous rather than banded.
seat.WORST_WHY: Nothing in it is lit. The orc at (210,10) carries no light; the frame is one flat value from corner to corner, with a drop shadow under the figure implying a ceiling light that doesn't exist anywhere else. The brown floor (x 55–245) is uniform speckle noise — blue and red flecks with no tile structure, no wear pattern, no direction. The grey "wall" band along the bottom (y 215–265) and the left column (x 0–55) are big flat slabs with hairline joints, drawn at the same texture density as a floor; only the 1-tile dark brick strip at y≈265 says "wall face", so the grey reads as raised floor, not wall. The same green moss stamp is placed unchanged at (30,60), (25,215), (365,160), (355,180) and once on the floor at (130,225). The pool (x 250–345) is a hard-edged rectangle with a honeycomb pattern and identical lily-pad stamps; it looks like a swimming pool. Projections are mixed: the chests at (65,5) and (65,50) are front-on with the lid open, the barrels at (120,195) and (170,195) are 3/4 with a visible side, the floor is straight top-down. It is a free tileset laid out on a grid.
seat.FLAGGED:

panel.ruling: five seats; block only on strong-majority regression (>=4 of 5 rank below the reference); else install if exit met and plant caught. Rank-in-deck cannot resolve polish-sized deltas at a 40% flip rate. — Rafe, 2026-09-09
panel.law: a gate's binding term must have a measured noise floor and must never be a single sample. — Rafe, 2026-09-08

_what: THE ITEM'S OWN MEASURED EXIT — required by INSTALL-LATEST (Rafe, 2026-09-08).
A build installs because it DID THE THING IT SET OUT TO DO. The rank test only says
the doing cost nothing against the seeded reference; this says what was done. Without
it, 'not worse than the reference' would mean 'not different from it', and a round
that changed nothing would install as readily as one that fixed something.
Declared here per item, recorded into the verdict, re-checked at the gate. The gate
refuses a `met` with no measurement behind it.

law: LOOP-PROCESS: an art round is judged by eyes on delivered frames. The plant must land worst-or-flagged; a passed plant voids the round and its findings are not read. The guards measure progress — rank in the deck — never rounds elapsed.
